html:
King of England from 1189 to 1199, called the Lionheart for his fame as a soldier. The son of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine, he grew up mostly in France and spent only about six months of his reign in England.

His father ruled the Angevin Empire, from the Scottish border to the Pyrenees. Richard rebelled against him with the help of the French king Philip II, and became king when Henry died.

He at once raised money for the Third Crusade, called after Saladin took Jerusalem in 1187. He took Acre and won at Arsuf in 1191, but could not retake Jerusalem, and in 1192 made a truce with Saladin that let Christian pilgrims visit the city. On the way home he was captured by Duke Leopold of Austria and handed to the emperor Henry VI, and England paid a huge ransom to free him.

He spent his last years fighting Philip for his French lands and died of a crossbow wound at the siege of Châlus. His brother John followed him, lost Normandy, and was forced to accept Magna Carta.
